title: The Tiny Sparrow and the Giant Forest Fire
hook: A tiny sparrow faces a giant forest fire with only a single drop of water in her beak.
question: Would you stay and help your home even if the task seemed impossible?
title_en: The Tiny Sparrow and the Giant Forest Fire
moral: No effort is too small when it is done with a big heart.
summary: A heartwarming tale of a tiny sparrow who inspires a whole forest to save their home. Learn how even the smallest act of courage can change the world.

scenes.text: Once in a vibrant forest lived a tiny sparrow named Piku. She was smaller than a mango leaf. Her wings were soft, and her heart was full of joy. Piku loved her home very much. She sang every morning for the tall trees and the clear river. The forest was her family. All the animals lived together in peace. Piku felt safe and happy in the shade of the ancient banyan tree.

That year, the summer was very harsh. The sun felt like a golden oven in the sky. The grass turned yellow and dry. The small ponds disappeared. Even the great river became a narrow stream. The leaves began to crackle and fall. Every creature felt tired and thirsty. Piku still sang, but her voice was a little faint. She hoped for the cool rain to visit their thirsty home very soon.

One afternoon, a dry branch rubbed against another. A tiny spark jumped onto the dry grass. Suddenly, a fire started spreading. It moved fast, like a hungry orange snake. The smoke rose high into the blue sky. The smell of burning wood filled the air. The animals grew very scared. They started running towards the far end of the forest. The peace of the green home was broken by the heat and fear.

The mighty elephants and the swift deer ran for their lives. The lions and tigers left their caves. Everyone was fleeing the heat and the smoke. Piku watched from a branch. She saw her beautiful home turning into ash. She saw the nests of other birds being destroyed. Her heart felt heavy with sadness. She did not want to leave. She wanted to protect the trees that had given her shade for so long.

Piku flew towards the river. It was a long way through the hot air. She dipped her tiny beak into the water. She carried just one drop of water. She flew back to the edge of the fire. She dropped that single drop onto the flames. The drop vanished instantly with a small hiss. Piku did not stop. She turned around and flew back to the river for another drop. She was determined to help.

An old elephant named Gajju saw Piku. He was standing safely on the other side of the river. He laughed a little and shook his head. He asked why a tiny bird was doing such a useless task. He told her that one drop of water could never put out a forest fire. He advised her to save her energy and fly away. Piku looked at him with steady eyes. She did not stop her work.

Piku replied that she knew she was small. She knew her drop was tiny. But she loved the forest. She told Gajju that she was doing what she could. She said that if everyone did their part, the world would be different. She flew back to the river again. Her wings were aching. Her feathers were covered in soot. Her throat was dry from the smoke. Still, she kept moving back and forth bravely.

The sun began to set, but the fire was still bright. Piku was very tired now. Her tiny legs were trembling. Her heart was beating very fast. Each trip to the river felt longer than the last. The heat was making it hard to breathe. But every time she saw a burning leaf, she remembered the cool shade. She thought of the little chicks in their nests. She found a new spark of strength inside.

Gajju the elephant watched her for a long time. He saw her courage. He felt a pinch in his heart. He looked at his own large trunk. He realized he could carry much more water than a sparrow. He felt ashamed of just watching. He walked to the river and filled his trunk. He ran to the fire and sprayed a huge cloud of water. The flames near the edge began to cool down immediately.

Other animals saw what Gajju was doing. They saw the tiny bird leading the way. A group of monkeys began to carry water in large leaves. The deer used their hooves to dig dirt to stop the fire. Even the squirrels helped by kicking sand onto the small flames. What started as one bird's effort became a village of help. Everyone worked together. No one was laughing anymore. They were all fighting for their home.

The collective effort started to work. The fire could not move forward. The animals worked through the night. The moon watched them from above. Slowly, the orange glow faded into gray smoke. The heat began to lower. By the time the first light of dawn appeared, the fire was almost gone. The forest was scarred, but it was safe. The trees were still standing. The animals were exhausted but very proud.

The next morning, a soft breeze blew. Dark clouds gathered in the sky. Finally, the rain began to fall. It washed away the ash and the soot. It cooled the thirsty ground. Piku sat on a wet branch, her wings heavy with rain. She was too tired to sing, but she was happy. She had saved her home. The big animals came to her. They thanked the tiny sparrow for teaching them a big lesson.

The forest eventually became green again. New shoots grew from the burnt earth. The flowers bloomed even brighter. Piku’s story was told to every new bird. They learned that no one is too small to make a difference. It does not matter how big the problem is. What matters is that we do our part with love. Today, Piku still sings in the ancient banyan tree. Her voice is the strongest in the whole forest.

kind: a Jataka style tale, retold freshly in your own words
